## Boundary-condition evidence {#sec-ch15-ch11}

Boundary tests must check the representation of the state as well as values in ghost cells.
This catalogue supports @sec-ch11, including characteristic outflow, walls and solids.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Connect the chapter's claims to executable assertions.

**Data.** Test inputs and thresholds; no new solver measurements.

**Placement.** Verification outside the simulation step.

**Activation.** Select the named tests; this catalogue changes no defaults.

**Guarantee / limits.** Source coverage does not establish a runtime pass.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer distinguishes report checks from solver tests.
:::

**Local symbols.** `v` and `r` below are state dictionaries for uninterrupted and restarted runs. Their `hydro_u` entries
contain conserved densities; `boundary_reference_w` stores primitive reference values with row-specific units.

### Derivation

The numerical derivations remain in the linked chapter. The error and conservation identities for interpreting
these tests are written out in the opening section of @sec-ch15; this inventory introduces no additional update equation.

1. Preserve the boundary reference across restart: `radiating.restart_continuation_and_missing_reference`
   saves a state and checks equality of the restored reference
   ({{< code tests/test_radiating_boundary.cpp radiating.restart_continuation_and_missing_reference >}}).
2. Continue both states for three steps. The same test requires exact equality of the conserved hydro and
   scalar arrays, so merely loading a checkpoint is not sufficient.
3. Remove the reference and repeat initialization. The test expects `c10::Error`; an old checkpoint without
   this state cannot silently count as the same radiating-boundary continuation.

Floating-point reduction bounds, with their assumptions, are derived in @sec-ch15.
They do not turn the inherited acceptance constants below into universal error bounds. Exact path, boolean
and equality contracts have no tolerance budget to enlarge.

### Numerical method

Read the assertion and its registration, then run the selected test in a build of the code pin.
Record device, precision, process count and skipped cases separately. @fig-ch15-evidence shows why an independent
formula check cannot establish that the compiled implementation ran.

#### How to use this evidence

From the repository root, replace `build` with the configured build of the code pin. First list the selection,
then run it; require a nonempty list and inspect skips in the output:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -C Release -N -R '^test_radiating_boundary\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -C Release --output-on-failure -R '^test_radiating_boundary\.release$'
```

For this ideal-gas restart case, `block_for` loads `test_radiating_boundary.yaml` and sets the EOS
({{< code tests/test_radiating_boundary.cpp block_for >}}). Use the shipped fixture rather than adding a new
activation key. The restart assertion deliberately refuses a checkpoint lacking `boundary_reference_w`.

The excerpt from `radiating.restart_continuation_and_missing_reference`
({{< code tests/test_radiating_boundary.cpp radiating.restart_continuation_and_missing_reference >}}) shows the assertion's inputs and contract:

```cpp
EXPECT_TRUE(torch::equal(v.at("hydro_u"), r.at("hydro_u")));
  EXPECT_TRUE(torch::equal(v.at("scalar_s"), r.at("scalar_s")));
  v.erase("boundary_reference_w");
  save_restart(v, b->cycle, path);
  EXPECT_THROW(restarted->initialize(r, path.c_str()), c10::Error);
```

The equality checks compare continuation states; deleting the reference tests the refusal path.
This is an exact restart contract, not a bound on the conservation residual in @eq-ch15-budget.

: Acceptance criteria read from the code pin; no solver pass is claimed. {#tbl-ch15-ch11-assertions}

The solid-segment acceptance thresholds are top-level assertions in
{{< code tests/test_implicit_stratified_solid.py >}}; `solid_run` constructs their inputs.
The curved-energy quantity is assembled by `curved_energy`
({{< code tests/test_implicit_stratified_solid.py curved_energy >}}).
The acceptance assertion is top-level code in the same file. It covers both spherical-polar and
gnomonic-equiangle cases; it is not restricted to the earlier spherical-polar-only inventory.
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py` retains the symbolic parity, acoustic inversion, admissibility,
corner averaging, partition, closure and wall-reference checks.

[C1] The restart assertion checks saved-reference equality, continued-state equality and rejection of a
missing reference. [C2] It does not replace the separate acoustic-reflection or CPU/CUDA assertions.[^ch15-ch11-five-choice]

### Limits

A mode or pulse test does not establish every outflow/implicit/well-balanced combination. Thin solid
geometries, scalar/diffusion coupling and stretched-wall convergence need separate evidence.
The explicit device comparison can skip CUDA; a skip is not a successful comparison.
